# browser-controller

> MCP server + Chrome extension that gives AI agents control of your real browser with existing sessions and logins.

## What it does

browser-controller is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server paired with a Chrome extension. It lets AI coding agents (Cursor, Claude, Windsurf, and any MCP client) interact with the user's actual browser - not a headless copy, not a new instance. The browser the user already has open, with their tabs, cookies, sessions, and logins intact.

## Key differentiator

Unlike Playwright MCP or Chrome DevTools MCP, which launch or attach to a separate browser, browser-controller controls the browser the user is already using. For projects with authentication, complex state, or corporate SSO, this means no re-login, no session setup, no cookie recreation.

## Tools (35 + 1 meta tool)

Every page tool takes a tabId from browser_tabs list (optional only on browser_navigate), so the agent never acts on the tab the user is looking at.

Reading: browser_observe (compact semantic observation whose snapshotId/refs feed browser_act), browser_snapshot (compact mode default - interactive elements only; source:"native" returns Chrome's own accessibility tree), browser_screenshot, browser_text (cheapest read), browser_find (find elements by natural-language description)
Interaction: browser_act (safe action on a browser_observe snapshot - rejects stale, hidden or covered targets), browser_click, browser_click_text, browser_type, browser_press_key, browser_scroll, browser_hover, browser_select, browser_wait, browser_fill_form, browser_drag, browser_upload_file
Chain, replay & record: browser_batch (several tool calls in one round-trip, stops at the first error), browser_shortcuts (save a flow with {{variables}}, replay it in one call), browser_gif (record the agent's actions in a tab as an animated GIF, clicks marked with a red ring; export writes the .gif and returns its path)
Navigation: browser_navigate, browser_tabs (list/create/close/focus/reload/lock/unlock), browser_resize_window, browser_emulate (offline/slow-3g network, CPU throttling, geolocation, dark mode, user agent), browser_list_browsers, browser_select_browser (several connected Chrome profiles)
JavaScript: browser_evaluate (DevTools-console style JS over CDP: top-level await, last expression returned), browser_run_action (self-contained JS action object via CDP)
Dialogs: browser_handle_dialog (answers the open alert/confirm/prompt; the action that opened it returns dialog:{type,message})
WebMCP: browser_webmcp_list (tools a page registers via document.modelContext or <form toolname>: name, schema, frame, annotations; supported:false when the page has none), browser_webmcp_call (call one with an input object instead of driving the UI; consequential tools and autosubmit forms need confirm:true; output is untrusted page data)
Debugging: browser_console (page console + uncaught errors with stacks since load, via the debugger; browser:true adds Chrome-reported messages and DevTools Issues), browser_network (type filter, requestId for redacted headers, captureBodies:true for response bodies), browser_intercept (block/redirect/add request headers per tab, per-tab mock responses the page really receives, capture ledger, HAR export), browser_inspect_element (computed styles, matching CSS rules with file:line and overridden declarations, event listeners incl. delegated)
Discovery: browser_tools (meta tool - list/search/activate tools; with BROWSER_CONTROLLER_PROGRESSIVE=1 only this tool is visible upfront: tool definitions drop from ~7,100 to ~170 tokens at startup; a task that activates 8 tools pays ~4,900 per request instead of ~7,300)

Full per-tool reference (parameters, behavior, timeouts): the "Tool reference" section of README.md.

## Architecture

- MCP server: Node.js/TypeScript, communicates with AI agent via stdio
- Chrome extension: Manifest V3, communicates with MCP server via WebSocket on localhost
- All communication is local. No cloud, no telemetry, no data exfiltration.

## Install

From source - this project is not published to npm (the npm package named "browser-controller" is an unrelated project) or the Chrome Web Store:

1. git clone https://github.com/compnew2006/browser-controller.git, then npm install and npm run build
2. MCP client config: command "node", args ["/absolute/path/to/browser-controller/mcp-server/dist/index.js"]
3. Chrome extension: Load unpacked from the extension/ directory, run npm run setup:pairing once, then reload the extension - it pairs itself with the daemon (manual fallback: paste the enrollment secret from ~/.browser-controller/enrollment.json into the popup) - see README.md "Quick Start"
